messages:
DevOps Bot: Planned maintenance - rolling edge router kernel update scheduled for 2026-03-19 02:00-02:45 UTC. This targets routing tables for EU and US clusters. Expected impact: short (1-2 min) TCP reconnects for active sessions. Posting draft statuspage and customer notice below.
Maya S.: Thanks — I’m oncall. I’ll own the window and watch the KV router metrics. Tagging Carlos for rollback plan.
Carlos R.: I’ve got rollback ready (script + snapshot). If we see >3% 1m error rate across frontends we abort and rollback.
Priya K.: Can we include a suggested customer-facing blurb that support can copy into tickets? Makes replies faster.
DevOps Bot: Draft statuspage: ```We will be performing a short rolling update of edge routing components on 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC. You may experience brief reconnects (under 2 minutes) for active inference requests. No data loss expected. We will update when complete.```
Jordan L.: Suggest adding: "If you experience sustained errors after 5 minutes, please contact support with request-id and region."
Maya S.: Updated statuspage copy with Jordan's line. Posting statuspage now -> statuspage.redwood.ai/incidents/4419802460 (internal link).
Priya K.: Customer notice (support template): "Heads up — we're doing a brief network routing update 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC that may cause short reconnects. Most calls will continue unaffected. If you see errors >5 minutes, reply with request-id and region and we'll escalate immediately." Can we add optional line about credits?
Jordan L.: Hold credits language for post-maint assessment. Only offer if we see visible customer impact.
Carlos R.: Oncall handoff: After the window finishes I’ll keep watch for 30m and then hand back to Maya. If any alarms fire I’ll page Maya and ops-sre.
Maya S.: Ack. I’ll set quiet-hours policy to prevent noisy alerts for brief reconnect spikes, but keep SLO threshold alarms enabled.
DevOps Bot: Incident bot note: preflight checks passed, disk and kernel patches staged on 60% of nodes. Starting rolling update at 02:00 UTC.
(02:04 UTC) Maya S.: First region (us-west1) rotated, brief reconnects observed, latency spike ~20s for a small percentage of requests, error rate peaked at 1.8% for 30s then recovered. No customer pages yet.
Carlos R.: Proceeding to eu-west1. Rolling window pace slowed to 30s between hosts to let caches warm.
(02:18 UTC) Maya S.: eu-west1 completed. Observed similar microspikes. All clear so far.
(02:39 UTC) DevOps Bot: Final region complete. Post-maint checks running (kv sync, routing convergence).
Carlos R.: Post-checks look green. No sustained error rates, latency back to baseline. Starting 30m watch as planned.
Priya K.: Drafting completion notice for customers: "Maintenance completed. If you experienced reconnects, please reply with request-id and region. If you have continued issues, we’ll prioritize a follow-up. Thanks for your patience."
Jordan L.: Thumbs up. Add link to support form and the statuspage entry.
Maya S.: I’ll mark statuspage as "resolved" in 10m unless we see any regressions. Handing off monitoring to Carlos for the next 30m.
Carlos R.: Oncall monitoring active. No pages during initial watch. Will update at end of watch with final health check and recommendation on credits.
(03:09 UTC) Carlos R.: Final check complete — no customer tickets tied to incident window, no SLO breaches detected. Recommend no automatic credits; if a customer reports impact we’ll evaluate case-by-case.
Priya K.: Noted. I’ll close the support template with the resolved copy and include a quick FAQ line: "Why did this happen? Routine router kernel update to improve stability — no data loss."
DevOps Bot: Maintenance complete. Status updated to resolved: statuspage.redwood.ai/incidents/4419802460.
Maya S.: Thanks team. Quick follow-up action: add a short runbook note about slowing rollout pace for future updates to reduce spikes. Filing a small PR to the ops-runbooks repo. :thumbsup:
